scope: K-Means Clustering & Association Pattern Mining over Multi-Crop Canonical v2

algorithm_comparison.practical_performance_assessment: Both FP-Growth and Apriori finish in less than 0.15 seconds on this dataset (2,596 transactions, 36 items). Output itemsets and rules are mathematically equivalent (difference = 0.0). Wall-clock differences at this scale are negligible in practice.

association_mining_evaluation.mode_a_leakage_status: VERIFIED ZERO LEAKAGE — Transaction matrix contains exclusively 36 discretized visual dummies.

research_conclusions.RQ1_Visual_Clustering: FINDING: Unsupervised K-Means demonstrates that K=2 is the metric-supported optimal clustering solution (Silhouette=0.4060, Davies-Bouldin=1.0990, Calinski-Harabasz=1154.38), cleanly partitioning the dataset into uniform, low-perimeter foliage (Cluster 1) versus textured, high-perimeter foliar surfaces (Cluster 0). K=4 provides an exploratory multi-phenotype sub-partition, though with substantially lower internal compactness (Silhouette=0.1651, Davies-Bouldin=1.8339). 2D PCA captures 52.11% of the total 32-feature variance.
research_conclusions.RQ2_Source_vs_Disease_Drivers: FINDING: Contingency analysis across both K=2 and K=4 reveals that cluster assignments correlate significantly with Health Status (Cramér's V = 0.4143 at K=2; V = 0.4326 at K=4) and Crop Species (V = 0.4725 at K=2; V = 0.3032 at K=4), while Dataset Source domain displays a lower association (V = 0.2211 at K=2; V = 0.2304 at K=4). This confirms that physiological lesion characteristics and foliar morphology dominate over imaging source bias.
research_conclusions.RQ3_Feature_Cooccurrence: FINDING: Mode A (Visual-Only) FP-Growth and Apriori discover 880 rules. High GLCM contrast and high lesion coverage consistently associate with low GLCM homogeneity (Lift > 2.1). High GLCM energy strongly co-occurs with high GLCM homogeneity (Lift = 2.58) in uniform leaf tissue. Mode B explores 272 label-conditioned rules separately.
research_conclusions.RQ4_Cross_Source_Stability: FINDING: Textural regularity (GLCM energy/homogeneity coupling) and necrotic contrast patterns appear consistently across both ICAR Rice and PlantDoc images, demonstrating feature stability across agricultural repositories.
